1401:
SHORT-CIRCUIT & OPEN-CIRCUIT — WHAT

CHANGES? (1)

THE GENERAL RULE · DC MACHINES · TRANSFORMERS, CT & PT

The general rule

SHORT circuit → resistance/impedance in that path ≈ 0 → current rises, unless the short also kills the field (shunt generator) — then everything collapses.

OPEN circuit → current in that path stops. If the open part was carrying opposing ampere-turns or a winding is cut by changing flux (CT secondary, synchronous-motor field at start), a dangerous high voltage appears.

Field winding rule: field opposing (differential) removed → flux ↑; field aiding (cumulative) removed → flux ↓; field lost in a motor → speed ↑↑ (N ∝ 1/φ).

Tests use this on purpose: short-circuit / blocked-rotor test → copper loss and impedance; open-circuit / no-load test → iron loss and magnetising current.

INDUCTION MOTOR · SYNCHRONOUS MACHINE

Induction motor

What is shorted / openedWhat happensWhy (cause → effect)
Slip-ring rotor terminals shortedNormal running (like a squirrel cage)Rotor circuit closed → rotor current → torque
Slip-ring rotor OPENNo torque — motor does not start; stator takes only magnetising currentNo rotor current → no torque (like an open-secondary transformer)
Rotor resistance shorted step by step during startSmooth acceleration, then normal runningHigh R at start → high Tst; removed at speed for efficiency
One supply phase OPEN while running (single phasing)Keeps running, current in other lines ↑ → overheatingRuns as a 1-φ motor; needs a single-phasing preventer
One supply phase OPEN at standstillDoes not start — only humsSingle-phase field gives no starting torque
Rotor blocked (blocked-rotor test)s = 1: at full V current is 5–7 ×; at reduced V gives copper loss and ZeqLike a transformer short-circuit test
No-load test (rotor free, no load)Small current → iron + friction lossesLike a transformer open-circuit test

Synchronous machine

What is shorted / openedWhat happensWhy (cause → effect)
